TRANSPORTATION NETWORK COMPANY DRIVER BACKGROUND CHECK REQUIREMENTS — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Lee · Acme Rides, Inc.

PURPOSE OF THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes the driver-screening requirements California law imposes specifically on transportation network companies (TNCs) — online-platform businesses such as rideshare companies — under Public Utilities Code sections 5431, 5445.2, and 5445.3, a distinct statutory scheme from the general consumer-reporting-agency background check requirements (FCRA, ICRAA) and the Fair Chance Act conviction-history rules addressed elsewhere in this corpus. It states facts about what these sections require of Acme Rides, Inc. before it contracts with, employs, or retains Jordan Lee as a participating driver. It does not itself conduct or report a background check, does not determine whether Jordan Lee meets or fails any statutory criterion, and does not tell Acme Rides, Inc. or Jordan Lee what to do about any particular background-check result.

WHO THESE SECTIONS COVER — “TRANSPORTATION NETWORK COMPANY” AND “PARTICIPATING DRIVER”
The Public Utilities Code defines a “participating driver” or “driver” as any person who uses a vehicle in connection with a transportation network company's online-enabled application or platform to connect with passengers. It defines a “transportation network company” broadly by function rather than by corporate form — an organization of any kind, including a corporation, limited liability company, partnership, or sole proprietor, operating in California that provides prearranged transportation services for compensation using an online-enabled application or platform to connect passengers with drivers using a personal vehicle. These definitions apply “for purposes of this article,” meaning Public Utilities Code Article 7 of Chapter 8 (sections 5430–5450), the article containing the driver background-check and licensing requirements described in this document.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "“Participating driver” or “driver” means any person who uses a vehicle in connection with a transportation network company’s online-enabled application or platform to connect with passengers."
  — Cal. Pub. Util. Code § 5431(a) (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Pub. Util. Code § 5431(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PUC&sectionNum=5431)
  "“Transportation network company” means an organization, including, but not limited to, a corporation, limited liability company, partnership, sole proprietor, or any other entity, operating in California that provides prearranged transportation services for compensation using an online-enabled application or platform to connect passengers with drivers using a personal vehicle."
  — Cal. Pub. Util. Code § 5431(c) (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Pub. Util. Code § 5431(c) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PUC&sectionNum=5431)
  Known gap: This clause quotes only the “participating driver” and “transportation network company” definitions in Public Utilities Code section 5431(a) and (c). It does not address the separate definitions in the same section for “personal vehicle,” “transportation network company insurance,” or “zero-emission vehicle,” and it does not independently verify how the California Public Utilities Commission's own regulatory decisions and general orders (which implement this article) may refine or apply these statutory terms in practice. It also does not determine whether any particular company or working arrangement meets this definition.

THE MANDATORY BACKGROUND CHECK — PUBLIC UTILITIES CODE § 5445.2(A)(1)
California law requires a transportation network company to conduct, or have a third party conduct, a local and national criminal background check for each participating driver. The check must include both the use of a multistate and multijurisdiction criminal records locator or other similar commercial nationwide database with validation, and a search of the United States Department of Justice National Sex Offender Public website. This is a background-check methodology requirement layered on top of, not a substitute for, the general California and federal background-check rules (ICRAA, FCRA, and the Fair Chance Act) addressed elsewhere in this corpus.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "A transportation network company shall conduct, or have a third party conduct, a local and national criminal background check for each participating driver that shall include both of the following:(A) The use of a multistate and multijurisdiction criminal records locator or other similar commercial nationwide database with validation.(B) A search of the United States Department of Justice National Sex Offender Public website."
  — Cal. Pub. Util. Code § 5445.2(a)(1) (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Pub. Util. Code § 5445.2(a)(1) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PUC&sectionNum=5445.2)
  Known gap: This clause quotes the statutory methodology requirement in Public Utilities Code section 5445.2(a)(1). The statute does not name specific approved commercial databases or vendors, does not state how frequently a background check must be repeated for a driver who continues to use the platform over time, and does not specify a maximum lookback period for the criminal records search itself (as opposed to the conviction-based disqualifications described in separate clauses of this document, which do carry stated time limits). Any California Public Utilities Commission general order or decision implementing this requirement in more operational detail was not independently verified for this document.

PERMANENT DISQUALIFICATION — SEX OFFENDER REGISTRATION AND SPECIFIED CONVICTIONS
California law bars a transportation network company from contracting with, employing, or retaining a driver who is currently registered on the United States Department of Justice National Sex Offender Public website, or who has been convicted of a violent felony as defined in Penal Code section 667.5, or of a violation of Penal Code section 236.1 (human trafficking), 11413, 11418, 11418.5, or 11419 (offenses involving weapons of mass destruction or related conduct). Unlike the seven-year lookback described elsewhere in this document, this bar is not stated to expire after any period of time.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "A transportation network company shall not contract with, employ, or retain a driver if the driver meets either of the following criteria:(A) Is currently registered on the United States Department of Justice National Sex Offender Public website.(B) Has been convicted of any of the following offenses:(i) A violent felony, as defined in Section 667.5 of the Penal Code.(ii) A violation of Section 236.1, 11413, 11418, 11418.5, or 11419 of the Penal Code."
  — Cal. Pub. Util. Code § 5445.2(a)(2) (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Pub. Util. Code § 5445.2(a)(2) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PUC&sectionNum=5445.2)
  Known gap: This clause quotes the cross-referencing text of Public Utilities Code section 5445.2(a)(2); it does not independently quote or verify the underlying definitions in Penal Code sections 667.5, 236.1, 11413, 11418, 11418.5, or 11419 that establish which specific offenses trigger this bar — those definitions were not separately fetched and verified for this document. It also does not describe how a transportation network company confirms “current” sex-offender registration status in practice, or what recourse, if any, exists to challenge a disqualification based on an inaccurate record.

THE SEVEN-YEAR LOOKBACK DISQUALIFIERS
Separately from the permanent bar, California law prohibits a transportation network company from contracting with, employing, or retaining a driver who has been convicted, within the previous seven years, of misdemeanor assault or battery, a domestic violence offense, driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs, or a felony violation of specified bribery, fraud, forgery, perjury, embezzlement, grand theft, or election-law offenses identified by statutory cross-reference to the Penal Code and Elections Code.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "A transportation network company shall not contract with, employ, or retain a driver if the driver has been convicted of any of the following offenses within the previous seven years:(A) Misdemeanor assault or battery.(B) A domestic violence offense.(C) Driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs.(D) A felony violation of Section 18540 of the Elections Code, or of Section 67, 68, 85, 86, 92, 93, 137, 138, 165, 518, or 530 of, subdivision (a) of Section 484 of, or subdivision (a) of Section 487 of, the Penal Code."
  — Cal. Pub. Util. Code § 5445.2(a)(3) (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Pub. Util. Code § 5445.2(a)(3) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PUC&sectionNum=5445.2)
  Known gap: This clause quotes the cross-referencing text of Public Utilities Code section 5445.2(a)(3). It does not independently quote or verify the specific Penal Code and Elections Code sections cross-referenced (Elections Code section 18540; Penal Code sections 67, 68, 85, 86, 92, 93, 137, 138, 165, 518, 530, 484(a), and 487(a)) to confirm exactly which conduct those sections define — those definitions were not separately fetched for this document. The statutory text quoted here does not itself state whether the seven-year period runs from the date of conviction, sentencing, or some other event; that computation question is not resolved by this clause.

OUT-OF-STATE CONVICTIONS COUNT, AND COMPANIES MAY IMPOSE STRICTER STANDARDS
The permanent bar and the seven-year lookback disqualifiers described elsewhere in this document are not limited to California convictions: they apply to a conviction of any offense committed in another jurisdiction that includes all of the elements of any of the disqualifying offenses. Separately, the statute confirms it does not prevent a transportation network company from imposing additional screening standards beyond what state law requires.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Paragraphs (2) and (3) apply with respect to a conviction of any offense committed in another jurisdiction that includes all of the elements of any of the offenses described or defined in those paragraphs."
  — Cal. Pub. Util. Code § 5445.2(a)(4) (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Pub. Util. Code § 5445.2(a)(4) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PUC&sectionNum=5445.2)
  "This section shall not be interpreted to prevent a transportation network company from imposing additional standards."
  — Cal. Pub. Util. Code § 5445.2(a)(5) (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Pub. Util. Code § 5445.2(a)(5) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PUC&sectionNum=5445.2)
  Known gap: This clause quotes Public Utilities Code section 5445.2(a)(4) and (a)(5). The statute does not itself state who performs the element-by-element comparison between an out-of-state offense and its California disqualifying-offense counterpart, or what happens when that comparison is disputed. This document does not identify what additional standards, if any, a particular transportation network company has chosen to impose — subdivision (a)(5) only confirms that companies are not barred from doing so.

THE PENALTY FOR NONCOMPLIANCE
A transportation network company that violates, or fails to comply with, Public Utilities Code section 5445.2 is subject to a penalty of not less than one thousand dollars ($1,000) nor more than five thousand dollars ($5,000) for each offense.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "A transportation network company that violates, or fails to comply with, this section is subject to a penalty of not less than one thousand dollars ($1,000) nor more than five thousand dollars ($5,000) for each offense."
  — Cal. Pub. Util. Code § 5445.2(b) (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Pub. Util. Code § 5445.2(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PUC&sectionNum=5445.2)
  Known gap: This clause quotes only the penalty amount stated in Public Utilities Code section 5445.2(b). It does not identify the enforcing body, the procedure for assessing or contesting a penalty, or whether “for each offense” means each disqualified driver, each violation of the check requirement, or some other unit — the statutory text does not define that phrase further. It does not address whether an individual driver or passenger has any private right of action distinct from this penalty provision, and it does not state whether the dollar amounts have been adjusted since the statute's last amendment.

A NARROW CARVE-OUT FROM ICRAA'S CONSUMER-REPORTING RULES
California's Investigative Consumer Reporting Agencies Act (ICRAA) normally restricts to whom an investigative consumer reporting agency may furnish a report. Public Utilities Code section 5445.2(c) creates a specific exception for transportation network company background checks: notwithstanding Civil Code section 1786.12, an investigative consumer reporting agency may furnish an investigative consumer report to a transportation network company about a person seeking to become a participating driver, regardless of whether that driver is to be an employee or an independent contractor of the company. The statute further states that Civil Code section 1786.18(a)(7) does not apply to a report furnished to a transportation network company under this exception.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Notwithstanding Section 1786.12 of the Civil Code, an investigative consumer reporting agency may furnish an investigative consumer report to a transportation network company about a person seeking to become a participating driver, regardless of whether the participating driver is to be an employee or an independent contractor of the transportation network company."
  — Cal. Pub. Util. Code § 5445.2(c)(1) (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Pub. Util. Code § 5445.2(c)(1) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PUC&sectionNum=5445.2)
  "Paragraph (7) of subdivision (a) of Section 1786.18 of the Civil Code does not apply to an investigative consumer report furnished to a transportation network company pursuant to paragraph (1)."
  — Cal. Pub. Util. Code § 5445.2(c)(2) (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Pub. Util. Code § 5445.2(c)(2) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PUC&sectionNum=5445.2)
  Known gap: This clause quotes only the cross-referencing exception language in Public Utilities Code section 5445.2(c); it does not independently quote or verify the underlying text of Civil Code section 1786.12 (the general list of permissible recipients of an investigative consumer report) or section 1786.18(a)(7) (the provision this exception disapplies) — neither was separately fetched for this document. This exception is narrow: it addresses only who may receive the report and one specific ICRAA provision; this clause does not establish that ICRAA's other requirements (such as disclosure and certification obligations, addressed in this corpus's separate ICRAA information sheet) cease to apply to a transportation network company's background check.

THE VALID DRIVER'S LICENSE REQUIREMENT
Separately from the criminal background check, California law requires a participating driver to possess a valid driver's license issued by the State of California, or, for a nonresident active-duty military member or their nonresident dependent, a valid driver's license issued by the state or territory of residence, subject to additional background-check and reporting conditions stated in the same section.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "A participating driver is required to possess either of the following:(1) A valid driver’s license issued by the State of California."
  — Cal. Pub. Util. Code § 5445.3(a)(1) (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Pub. Util. Code § 5445.3(a)(1) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PUC&sectionNum=5445.3)
  Known gap: This clause quotes Public Utilities Code section 5445.3(a)(1), the general California-license requirement, but does not quote the full nonresident-military-member exception and its accompanying conditions in section 5445.3(a)(2), or the notice-of-Vehicle-Code-provisions requirement in section 5445.3(b). The statute does not require a commercial driver's license or any particular license class or endorsement; this clause does not address vehicle-specific licensing requirements that may exist under other law.

SIGNATURE AND CERTIFICATION
Please sign below to indicate receipt and review of this information sheet.

Participating driver / applicant: Jordan Lee
Position: Participating Driver
Date: September 6, 2026

Acme Rides, Inc. certifies that this information sheet was provided to Jordan Lee.

Company representative: _______________
Date: September 6, 2026
